skill.name: gen-paylink-govilo
skill.description: Upload user-selected files to Govilo and create paid unlock links through the Govilo Bot API. The skill packages inputs, uploads a ZIP through a presigned URL, and returns the created unlock link.
skill.summary: Create Govilo paid unlock links from ZIPs, folders, or files.
skill.author: hau823823

security_audit.summary: Confirmed risks include remote installer commands that pipe downloaded scripts into shells, Govilo API key handling, external file upload, and unsafe temporary ZIP path creation. Many static hits in markdown tables, error-code documentation, and dedicated env-file warnings are false positives. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installers are executed directly from downloaded scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell and irm-to-iex instructions with package-manager installs or checksum-verified downloads.

remediation.issue: The CLI workflow uploads local files to Govilo-managed storage.
remediation.suggestion: Require a final confirmation that lists exact paths, file count, size, destination, title, price, and seller address.

remediation.issue: Govilo API keys are required and passed into outbound API requests.
remediation.suggestion: Keep keys only in a dedicated Govilo env file, mask them in logs, and avoid accepting secrets through command history.

remediation.issue: Temporary ZIP paths are created with tempfile.mktemp.
remediation.suggestion: Use mkstemp, NamedTemporaryFile, or TemporaryDirectory with restrictive permissions and reliable cleanup.

remediation.issue: The skill can create paid links for arbitrary uploaded content.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear user prompts requiring ownership, licensing, and approval before monetizing uploaded files.

content.value_statement: Selling a file through Govilo requires packaging, upload, and item creation. This skill automates those steps and returns a paid unlock link.
actual_capabilities: Reads a Govilo API key and seller address from a dedicated environment file or command option.
Accepts a ZIP file, a folder, or repeated file paths as input.
Packages non-ZIP inputs into a ZIP archive before upload.
Requests a Govilo presigned upload URL and uploads the archive.
Creates a Govilo item with a title, price, and optional description.
Returns the created unlock link and item metadata after a successful upload.
limitations: Requires a Govilo API key and a Base-chain seller address before use.
Limits uploads to 20 MB and 20 files.
Uploads selected files to a third-party service controlled by Govilo.
Does not verify content ownership, licensing, taxes, or buyer support terms.

use_cases.title: Sell a digital download
use_cases.description: Package a finished file and create a Govilo unlock link with a USDC price.

use_cases.title: Prepare client delivery
use_cases.description: Bundle approved project files and publish a paid delivery link for a client.

use_cases.title: Automate repeat uploads
use_cases.description: Use the CLI workflow to create consistent Govilo items from prepared release folders.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple link
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner upload of one prepared ZIP file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Govilo unlock link for this ZIP. Ask me for the title, USDC price, description, and seller address before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Package a folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Upload a folder that needs automatic ZIP packaging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Package this folder and create a Govilo paid link. Confirm the folder path and list the files before upload.

prompt_templates.title: Use an existing seller address
prompt_templates.scenario: Repeated creator workflow with a dedicated environment file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Govilo link using my dedicated Govilo environment file. Confirm the title, price, description, and input path first.

prompt_templates.title: Review before monetizing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow requiring a safety check before upload.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the selected files, confirm they should be uploaded to Govilo, then create the paid unlock link with the agreed price.

output_examples.input: A creator asks for a paid link for a prepared course archive priced at 15 USDC.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the file, title, price, and seller address, then returns the new Govilo unlock link.

output_examples.input: A freelancer provides a delivery folder and wants a paid client access link.
output_examples.output: The skill packages the folder, uploads the archive, creates the Govilo item, and reports the link and file count.

output_examples.input: A user is missing the Govilo API key or seller address.
output_examples.output: The skill explains which required value is missing and points the user to the setup guide.

best_practices: Use a dedicated Govilo environment file that contains only Govilo credentials.
Review every file path before upload because the archive leaves the local machine.
Confirm the seller address, title, price, and description before creating the item.
anti_patterns: Do not use a shared project environment file with unrelated secrets.
Do not upload private, unlicensed, or unapproved files to create a paid link.
Do not run remote installer commands without reviewing a safer installation path.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Govilo paid unlock link for a ZIP, folder, or selected files.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: It needs a Govilo API key and a Base-chain seller address.

faq.question: Where are files uploaded?
faq.answer: Files are uploaded through a Govilo presigned URL to Govilo-managed storage.

faq.question: Can it package folders automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It zips a folder or multiple files before upload.

faq.question: What upload limits apply?
faq.answer: The documented limits are 20 MB and 20 files.

faq.question: Does it verify content rights?
faq.answer: No. Users must confirm they have permission to upload and sell the selected files.
